relationships.title: Proposed Vows and Procedure for Transferring Church Membership

metadata.summary: A Southeast Alabama overture adding transfer-of-membership procedures was in conflict because it equated 'profession of faith' with doctrinal subscription and contained internal procedural contradictions.

relationships.title: BCO 38-3 - Removing Members from the Roll
relationships.disposition: advice given — no constitutional bar to accepting resignation

metadata.summary: The CCB advised there is no constitutional bar preventing a court from accepting a member's resignation and removing that person's name from the roll.

relationships.title: BCO 38-3 - Removing Members from the Roll
relationships.disposition: declined to advise; reference returned as improper

metadata.summary: The CCB declined to advise, finding the reference improper, but noted that GA Judicial Case 93-3 does not bar full formal discipline of a member who tenders a letter of resignation.

relationships.title: Voluntary association principle applied to individual church membership

metadata.summary: The CCB affirmed that the principle of voluntary association governing churches also applies to individuals joining a local PCA congregation.

relationships.title: Voluntary resignation from membership and application of BCO 46-5

metadata.summary: The GA clarified that BCO 46-5 had been variously interpreted regarding voluntary resignation, resolving that a simple resignation does not automatically trigger the willful-neglect excommunication process.

relationships.title: Membership status and session authority upon dissolution of a congregation

metadata.summary: Upon dissolution of a congregation, the session terminates, membership in the visible church is dissolved for those not transferred, and Presbytery may not unilaterally assign members to other churches.

relationships.title: Whether a resignation letter constitutes willful neglect justifying roll erasure

metadata.summary: The committee referred Stony Point's questions about non-judicial removal to earlier General Assembly answers and Overture 5. The related Overture 5 report treated easier roll erasure as equivalent to excommunication and referred possible BCO amendments for later consideration.

relationships.title: Member resignation, transfer during discipline, and definition of willful neglect

metadata.summary: The CCB ruled that the BCO provides no mechanism for voluntary membership resignation, that original session jurisdiction controls transfers during discipline, and that 'willful neglect' is defined by the session subject to higher-court review.

relationships.title: Procedure for removing members who relocate without affiliating elsewhere

metadata.summary: BCO 46-2 governs removal of members who move away and fail to affiliate within a year; BCO 46-5's formal discipline applies only to willful neglect, not mere relocation.

relationships.title: Whether deletion from the roll under BCO 46-5 constitutes excommunication

metadata.summary: The CCB answered yes — 'deletion' under BCO 46-5 is excommunication in effect, and the due-process procedures of BCO 27-5 must therefore be followed.

relationships.title: Whether refusing to join an available church constitutes willful neglect

metadata.summary: The CCB declined to rule, leaving the session as court of original jurisdiction to determine the gravity of a member's refusal to affiliate with an available evangelical church.

relationships.title: Meaning of willful neglect and gross crime under BCO 46-5 and 30-4

metadata.summary: BCO 46-5 requires due process under BCO 27-5 for incorrigible members, and 'gross crime or heresy' is to be understood in its biblical and moral sense as determined by the church court.

The judicial panel denied the complaint on the grounds that the Session retained discretion to determine the timing of discipline proceedings, and procedural errors did not result in material prejudice.

relationships.title: Melton et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery

topics: higher court authority over local church
metadata.synopsis: Complainants challenged the ruling of the session of Westminster Presbyterian Church (Chattanooga) disallowing proxy votes at a December 10, 1989 congregational meeting that voted not to rescind the earlier dissolution and property transfer to New City Fellowship. The SJC denied all specifications, holding that proxy voting was not required under BCO 24-4 or Robert's Rules, and that the congregation's decision to dissolve was within its rights under BCO Chapter 25.

relationships.title: TE John T. DeBardeleben v. Philadelphia Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: - **g.** He proposed erasing the names of those who lost the vote on Feb. 4, 1987 from the roll of the church without due process. (cf. BCO 46-5)

metadata.synopsis: A complaint challenged Philadelphia Presbytery’s approval of proceedings that cleared teaching and ruling elders without properly trying serious public accusations arising from Christ Church’s division. All three specifications were sustained because plea bargaining, dropped charges, and failure to hear necessary witnesses left the accusations unresolved. Presbytery’s action was annulled and de novo trials produced mixed convictions and acquittals. Harold Burkhart received six months’ suspension, Douglas McCready an admonition, and six former ruling elders three-month suspensions. The decision stressed taking such conflicts to Presbytery or judicial process rather than the congregation.
